mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters indicates strong economic demand, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of instances following sustained GDP growth, or GDP growth does not lead to a statistically significant increase in SPX returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points within a month signals a tightening labor market, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending is expected to increase.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production over two consecutive months signals increased economic activity, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances following sustained industrial production growth, or industrial production growth does not lead to a statistically significant increase in SPX returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 5% within two months signals increased consumer demand, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as related industries benefit.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between housing starts increase and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and the CPI is increasing, it signals a period of high inflation and tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
regime_hint: high inflation and tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and increasing CPI on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreases, it signals a strong labor market, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending is expected to increase.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of increasing PAYEMS and decreasing UNRATE on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures by more than 1% within a month signals reduced consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between RSAFS decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
